conceptCapsule.title: Kinetic Friction, Surface Deformation & Multi-Body Friction
conceptCapsule.summary: 1. Kinetic Friction: Operates whenever relative sliding occurs between contacting surfaces ($f_k = \mu_k N$). It is nearly independent of relative sliding velocity and acts strictly opposite to relative velocity. 2. Rolling Friction: Arises from asymmetric normal pressure distribution caused by microscopic elastic/inelastic deformation at the contact patch. $\mu_{\text{rolling}} \ll \mu_k < \mu_s$. 3. Two-Block Systems: In stacked blocks $(m_1\text{ on }m_2)$, determine the maximum possible acceleration without slipping ($a_{\text{max}}$) governed by the limiting friction at the interface before deciding whether the bodies move together or slide relative to each other. 4. Incline Ascent/Descent: Acceleration during upward projection is $a_{\text{up}} = g(\sin\theta + \mu_k\cos\theta)$ while downward acceleration is $a_{\text{down}} = g(\sin\theta - \mu_k\cos\theta)$, leading to $t_{\text{down}} > t_{\text{up}}$.
conceptCapsule.keyFormula: $$f_k = \mu_k N, \quad a_{\text{up}} = g(\sin\theta + \mu_k\cos\theta), \quad a_{\text{down}} = g(\sin\theta - \mu_k\cos\theta), \quad P_{\text{dissipated}} = f_k v_{\text{rel}}$$
conceptCapsule.examTrap: Kinetic friction always opposes the *relative* velocity between the two contacting surfaces, NOT necessarily the motion of the body with respect to the ground. For example, a moving conveyor belt accelerates a resting box forward via kinetic friction until their velocities equalize.

questions.statement: A block of mass $m = 2\text{ kg}$ is sliding along a rough horizontal floor with an initial speed of $v_0 = 10\text{ m/s}$. If the coefficient of kinetic friction is $\mu_k = 0.25$, the distance travelled by the block before it comes to rest is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
1. Kinetic friction: $f_k = \mu_k mg = 0.25 \times 2 \times 10 = 5\text{ N}$.
2. Deceleration: $a = \mu_k g = 0.25 \times 10 = 2.5\text{ m/s}^2$.
3. Stopping distance: $s = \frac{v_0^2}{2a} = \frac{100}{2 \times 2.5} = 20\text{ m}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: Which of the following correctly describes the fundamental origin of rolling friction between a rolling wheel and the ground?

options.text: Relative sliding velocity at the point of contact
Local deformation of the contacting surfaces causing asymmetry in the normal reaction line
Air drag acting on the top half of the wheel

questions.solution:
Rolling friction arises due to micro-deformations at the contact region, which shifts the line of action of the normal reaction slightly forward, producing a counter-torque opposing rotation.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A block slides down a rough inclined plane of inclination $\theta = 45^\circ$ with constant velocity. The coefficient of kinetic friction $\mu_k$ between the block and the plane is:
questions.solution:
Constant velocity implies zero net acceleration: $mg\sin\theta - \mu_k mg\cos\theta = 0 \implies \mu_k = \tan\theta = \tan 45^\circ = 1.0$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A block takes twice as long to slide down a rough $45^\circ$ inclined plane as it does to slide down an identical smooth $45^\circ$ inclined plane. The coefficient of kinetic friction $\mu_k$ of the rough plane is:
questions.solution:
1. Acceleration on smooth plane: $a_1 = g\sin 45^\circ$. Acceleration on rough plane: $a_2 = g(\sin 45^\circ - \mu_k\cos 45^\circ) = g\sin 45^\circ(1 - \mu_k)$.
2. Since $s = \frac{1}{2}at^2$, $t \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{a}} \implies \frac{t_2}{t_1} = \sqrt{\frac{a_1}{a_2}} = 2 \implies \frac{a_1}{a_2} = 4$.
3. $\frac{1}{1 - \mu_k} = 4 \implies 1 - \mu_k = 0.25 \implies \mu_k = 0.75$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A block of mass $m_1 = 2\text{ kg}$ is placed on top of another block of mass $m_2 = 3\text{ kg}$. The coefficient of static friction between the blocks is $\mu_s = 0.4$, and the floor beneath $m_2$ is frictionless. The maximum horizontal force $F$ that can be applied to the lower block $m_2$ so that both blocks move together without slipping is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
1. Upper block $m_1$ is driven forward purely by friction: $f_{s1}^{\text{max}} = \mu_s m_1 g = 0.4 \times 2 \times 10 = 8\text{ N}$.
2. Maximum allowable common acceleration: $a_{\text{max}} = \frac{f_{s1}^{\text{max}}}{m_1} = \mu_s g = 4\text{ m/s}^2$.
3. Total mass system: $F_{\text{max}} = (m_1 + m_2) a_{\text{max}} = (2 + 3) \times 4 = 20\text{ N}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: In Question 5, if the horizontal force applied to the lower block $m_2$ is $F = 30\text{ N}$, the acceleration of the upper block $m_1$ ($\mu_k = 0.3$) and the lower block $m_2$ are respectively:
questions.solution:
Since $F = 30\text{ N} > F_{\text{max}} = 20\text{ N}$, slipping occurs between the blocks.
Kinetic friction: $f_k = \mu_k m_1 g = 0.3 \times 2 \times 10 = 6\text{ N}$.
Upper block acceleration: $a_1 = \frac{f_k}{m_1} = \frac{6}{2} = 3\text{ m/s}^2$.
Lower block acceleration: $a_2 = \frac{F - f_k}{m_2} = \frac{30 - 6}{3} = 8\text{ m/s}^2$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A block of mass $m_1 = 4\text{ kg}$ rests on a slab of mass $m_2 = 6\text{ kg}$ on a smooth floor. The coefficient of friction between $m_1$ and $m_2$ is $\mu_s = 0.5$. If a horizontal force $F = 12\text{ N}$ is applied to the upper block $m_1$, the frictional force acting on the slab $m_2$ is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
1. Maximum static friction: $f_s^{\text{max}} = 0.5 \times 4 \times 10 = 20\text{ N}$.
2. Max acceleration of lower slab: $a_{\text{max}} = \frac{20}{6} = 3.33\text{ m/s}^2$.
3. Threshold force on $m_1$ for slipping: $F_{\text{threshold}} = (4 + 6)(3.33) = 33.3\text{ N}$.
4. Since $F = 12\text{ N} < 33.3\text{ N}$, both bodies accelerate together: $a_{\text{common}} = \frac{12}{10} = 1.2\text{ m/s}^2$.
5. Static friction driving $m_2$: $f = m_2 a_{\text{common}} = 6 \times 1.2 = 7.2\text{ N}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: Which of the following relations correctly ranks the magnitude of friction coefficients under identical contact surface conditions?
questions.solution:
Static friction coefficient is highest due to interlocking of asperities, followed by kinetic friction during sliding, while rolling friction coefficient is by far the lowest (typically two orders of magnitude smaller): $\mu_s > \mu_k > \mu_{\text{rolling}}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A conveyor belt moves horizontally with a constant speed $v = 4\text{ m/s}$. A box is gently placed on the belt with zero initial speed. If $\mu_k = 0.2$, the distance travelled by the box relative to the ground before it stops slipping on the belt is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
1. Forward acceleration: $a = \mu_k g = 0.2 \times 10 = 2\text{ m/s}^2$.
2. Slipping ceases when speed reaches $v = 4\text{ m/s}$.
3. Distance relative to ground: $s_{\text{ground}} = \frac{v^2}{2a} = \frac{4^2}{2(2)} = 4\text{ m}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: In Question 9, the distance travelled by the box relative to the belt during the slipping phase is:
questions.solution:
1. Time to match speeds: $t = \frac{v}{a} = \frac{4}{2} = 2\text{ s}$.
2. Belt displacement: $s_{\text{belt}} = v \times t = 4 \times 2 = 8\text{ m}$.
3. Relative displacement (skid mark length): $s_{\text{rel}} = s_{\text{belt}} - s_{\text{ground}} = 8 - 4 = 4\text{ m}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A block of mass $m$ is projected with speed $v_0$ up a rough inclined plane of angle $	heta$ ($\mu_k < \tan\theta$). The ratio of the time of ascent $t_{\text{up}}$ to the time of descent $t_{\text{down}}$ back to the starting point is:
questions.solution:
Ascent deceleration: $a_{\text{up}} = g(\sin\theta + \mu_k\cos\theta)$.
Descent acceleration: $a_{\text{down}} = g(\sin\theta - \mu_k\cos\theta)$.
Since travel distance $s$ along incline is identical: $t = \sqrt{\frac{2s}{a}} \implies \frac{t_{\text{up}}}{t_{\text{down}}} = \sqrt{\frac{a_{\text{down}}}{a_{\text{up}}}} = \sqrt{\frac{\sin\theta - \mu_k\cos\theta}{\sin\theta + \mu_k\cos\theta}}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A block of mass $M = 10\text{ kg}$ is placed on a rough horizontal surface with $\mu_k = 0.2$. A horizontal force $F(t) = 4t\text{ N}$ (where $t$ is in seconds) is applied starting from $t = 0$. The speed of the block at $t = 10\text{ s}$ is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, assume $\mu_s = \mu_k$):
questions.solution:
1. Frictional resistance: $f = \mu_k Mg = 0.2 \times 100 = 20\text{ N}$.
2. Block starts moving when $F(t) = 20 \implies 4t_0 = 20 \implies t_0 = 5\text{ s}$.
3. For $t \ge 5\text{ s}$, $a(t) = \frac{4t - 20}{10} = 0.4t - 2$.
4. Velocity at $t = 10\text{ s}$: $v = \int_5^{10}(0.4t - 2)dt = [0.2t^2 - 2t]_5^{10} = (20 - 20) - (5 - 10) = 5\text{ m/s}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A heavy block of mass $m$ is pulled with a constant horizontal force $F > \mu_k mg$ across a rough horizontal floor. The rate of heat energy dissipated by kinetic friction as the block moves with speed $v$ is:
questions.solution:
Rate of heat dissipation equals the power dissipated by the kinetic friction force: $P = f_k v = (\mu_k mg)v$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A small coin rests on a horizontal turntable at a distance $r = 20\text{ cm}$ from the axis of rotation. The coefficient of static friction between the coin and the turntable is $\mu_s = 0.5$. The maximum angular speed $\omega$ of the turntable at which the coin does not slip is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
Static friction provides required centripetal acceleration: $m\omega^2 r \le \mu_s mg \implies \omega_{\text{max}} = \sqrt{\frac{\mu_s g}{r}} = \sqrt{\frac{0.5 \times 10}{0.2}} = \sqrt{25} = 5.0\text{ rad/s}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A chain of length $L$ and mass $M$ is held on a rough horizontal table such that a length $y$ hangs over the edge. If the coefficient of static friction between the chain and the table is $\mu_s$, the maximum fraction $y/L$ of the chain that can hang over without sliding is:
questions.solution:
Hanging weight = $\left(\frac{M}{L}y\right)g$. Friction on table = $\mu_s \left(\frac{M}{L}(L - y)\right)g$.
Balancing for limiting state: $\frac{M}{L}yg = \mu_s\frac{M}{L}(L - y)g \implies y = \mu_s(L - y) \implies \frac{y}{L} = \frac{\mu_s}{1 + \mu_s}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A plank of mass $M$ is placed on a smooth horizontal floor. A block of mass $m$ is projected with speed $u$ on the top surface of the plank ($\mu_k$ between block and plank). The common final velocity of the block and the plank when relative slipping ceases is:
questions.solution:
Friction between block and plank is internal to the (block + plank) system. With no external horizontal force, linear momentum is conserved: $m u = (M + m)v_{\text{common}} \implies v_{\text{common}} = \frac{m u}{M + m}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: In Question 16, the total mechanical energy converted into heat due to kinetic friction between the block and plank during the process is:
questions.solution:
Loss in kinetic energy $\Delta K = K_i - K_f = \frac{1}{2}mu^2 - \frac{1}{2}(M + m)\left(\frac{mu}{M+m}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{Mm}{M+m}\right)u^2 = \frac{1}{2}\mu_{\text{reduced}} u^2$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A block of mass $m = 2\text{ kg}$ is kept on a rough inclined plane of angle $30^\circ$ ($\mu_s = 0.6, \mu_k = 0.5$). A force $F$ is applied parallel to the incline upward. The minimum value of $F$ to prevent the block from sliding down is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2, \sqrt{3} \approx 1.73$):
questions.solution:
Downhill gravity component: $mg\sin 30^\circ = 20 \times 0.5 = 10\text{ N}$.
Max static friction available: $f_s^{\text{max}} = \mu_s mg\cos 30^\circ = 0.6 \times 20 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 6\sqrt{3} \approx 10.39\text{ N}$.
Since $f_s^{\text{max}} > mg\sin 30^\circ$, friction alone holds the block at rest. Thus minimum external force required is $0\text{ N}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A solid cylinder of mass $M$ and radius $R$ rolls without slipping down an inclined plane of angle $	heta$. The magnitude and direction of the static frictional force acting on the cylinder is:
questions.solution:
Translational dynamics: $Mg\sin\theta - f_s = Ma$.
Rotational dynamics: $f_s R = I\alpha = \left(\frac{1}{2}MR^2\right)\left(\frac{a}{R}\right) \implies f_s = \frac{1}{2}Ma$.
Solving together: $a = \frac{2}{3}g\sin\theta \implies f_s = \frac{1}{3}Mg\sin\theta$, acting uphill.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A car travels at speed $v$ on a flat horizontal road. The coefficient of static friction between the tyres and the road is $\mu_s$. The minimum stopping distance without skidding (using maximum static friction) is:
questions.solution:
Maximum braking deceleration without skidding: $a_{\text{max}} = \mu_s g$.
Using $v^2 = 2 a s \implies s_{\text{min}} = \frac{v^2}{2\mu_s g}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.
